# Porting an xscreensaver hack

The rules live in `AGENTS.md` ("Rules", "Gotchas") and the path-scoped notes in
`.claude/rules/`. This skill sets the order of work and the points to stop. The
numbered steps are in `adding-a-hack.md` and the recipes it names are in
`techniques.md`, both next to this file. For several hacks in one go, read
`batches.md` too.

## 1. Pick, then read the source

Take S-rated rows from `docs/porting-assessment.md` first, and prefer a low
**Speed** band: the table runs each unported S hack on the host. The effort
rating counts missing shim calls, not memory, speed or stack (Braid was S, and
would have shown as high). A high band is a hack that will probably run slowly
on the board; a low band is not a guarantee, because a hack still doing
software `double` maths runs far slower on the device than on the host. Read
the hack's source before copying it, and look for:

| The source has | Technique (seen in) |
| --- | --- |
| Arrays or a state over a few MB | Build-time patch (Maze) |
| `sin`, `cos`, `sqrt`, `pow`, `double` in a hot loop | Single precision (Galaxy, Substrate) |
| Locals over a few KB | Stack check (Rorschach) |
| An allocation of 100 KB or more, or `exit()` on failure | Large allocations (Substrate) |
| Pixmaps, clip masks, a logo image | Images (Maze) |
| A hack that restarts itself | Restart leak test (Maze, Substrate) |
| A `free` that relies on state `draw` sets up (a lazy `initted`) | Stopping before the first draw (Blaster) |
| Hairlines, fades or `glPolygonOffset` in a GL hack | Thin lines in a GL hack |
| Threads, GL, Xft, shared memory | Skipping a hack |
| A licence header | Read it; add a notices section only if it differs from jwz's |

## 2. Set up

Work in a worktree off `origin/main`. Its setup and the commands it refuses are
in "Worktree setup".

## 3. Red, copy, green

Follow `adding-a-hack.md`. Show the registry test failing before
copying. Fill each shim gap test-first, then break the code on purpose and
watch the test fail ("Tests that cannot be fooled"). Filling a missing
function is a shim gap. Changing what every hack sees (the runner, a default, a
shared helper) is not: stop and ask Rod first. A speed-up in the shared GL
layer counts too, even when every pinned frame hash still matches (HexTrail's
deferred depth clear): ask before writing it, and name it in the PR body.

## 4. Verify on the host

Run `pio test -e native`, `uv run --with pytest --with pillow pytest tools/tests`
and `uv run tools/check_notices.py`, and dump frames at several counts. Host
frames cannot show a byte swap, which happens in the push to the display: judge
colour on the device, on a colour you know the answer to.

## 5. Device

Flash only after Rod says so in this conversation; approval for one flash is
not approval for the next. See "Device capture". Report "compiles", "host tests
pass" and "runs on the device" separately; only Rod can say what the screen
shows. If it is slow, measure, change one thing, flash again and compare; if it
is still slow, say so and suggest dropping it. A hack that runs at a good rate
can still go: Rod dropped Boing (8.3 fps, "pretty boring on a small screen")
and asked for HexTrail to be tuned because it fell under 10 fps before the
rotation moved on. Judge a hack on a 466 px round screen, and by its worst
window as well as its mean. Record the numbers in
`tools/assessment_measured.md.in`, marking anything unmeasured as such.

## 6. Deliver

Commit named paths. Open the draft PR with `entire trail create` and put what
is unverified in its body. After a rebase, a push needs `--force-with-lease`:
ask Rod each time. Rod approves and merges; then delete the branch and
fast-forward `main`. New gotchas go in the matching `.claude/rules/` file (or
`AGENTS.md` if they apply everywhere) in the same PR, and deferred
ideas become issues.

## Red flags

| Thought | Reality |
| --- | --- |
| "It is rated S, so I need not read it" | Maze was rated L for Xlib gaps; the real blocker was a 20 MB `calloc`. |
| "It compiles, so it works" | Rorschach compiled and rebooted on its first frame. |
| "The colours look right" | Not from a host frame: every hack was byte swapped until Maze. |
| "My test passes, so it tests something" | A test through Pyro passed with the runner broken. Break the code on purpose. |
| "AGENTS.md says to fix shim gaps, so I can change the runner" | A new function is a gap. A change every hack sees needs Rod. |
| "Rod approved flashing earlier" | Ask again for each flash. |
| "Single precision is done, so the hack is as fast as it gets" | HexTrail gained 0.3 fps from it and 2.3 from a depth clear in the GL layer. Read what the shared code does each frame. |
| "The mean is above 10 fps" | HexTrail's mean was 15.3 and its worst window 10.8; its step grew all cycle. Read the lowest window. |

# X11 shim and framework gotchas

Moved verbatim from the Gotchas section of AGENTS.md.

- `unsigned long` is 4 bytes on the device and 8 on the host, so a hack that
  allocates arrays of it (Substrate's two 466 by 466 buffers) is twice the size
  on the host, and host leak numbers are twice the device's. On the device,
  plain `malloc`/`realloc` of about 868 KB reached PSRAM (free PSRAM fell by
  1.74 MB) and came back on restart; internal heap barely moved.
- The board's `malloc` is `CONFIG_SPIRAM_USE_MALLOC=y` with
  `SPIRAM_MALLOC_ALWAYSINTERNAL=4096`: a block up to 4 KB comes from internal
  RAM and falls back to PSRAM when that is full, and a bigger one goes to PSRAM
  first. An allocation fails only when PSRAM is gone, so a hack's `abort()` on
  a failed allocation is not the risk it looks. The cost of a big pattern is
  internal heap drained to near zero (Celtic read 1,792 B free) and its data
  in slower PSRAM: compare the log's `psram=` with its idle value for the
  overflow.
- `erase_window` (`erase.c`) follows upstream's contract: the first call draws
  nothing and returns a state, so a hack that waits after it (Celtic's 5 s
  `*delay2`) waits on the finished picture. The second call starts a one-second
  wipe (blinds, circle, fizzle or random lines, picked at random), each later
  call draws the next step, and the call after the second is up clears the
  window and returns NULL. Progress comes from `double_time()`, not from the
  call count, so the wipe lasts a second at any step rate. A test or tool
  that does not sleep for a hack's delay must install a clock
  (`xshim_set_clock`), or a wipe never ends. Six hacks never call
  `eraser_free`, so the display tracks live states and the runner releases
  them when a hack stops.
- xlockmore hacks (the 40 that include `xlockmore.h`) need `-DSTANDALONE`,
  which every PlatformIO env and `score_hacks.py` set; without it they
  include `xlock.h` instead. The envs also define `HAVE_MOBILE`, because
  otherwise each hack's `XSCREENSAVER_LINK` defines the same global
  `xscreensaver_function_table` and two hacks fail to link; the only other
  effect is an inert `*ignoreRotation: True` default. Register one in
  `hacks/registry.c` with `XLOCKMORE_HACK(<name>, "<Class>")`. The runner runs
  the hack's `setup_cb` once and passes `setup_arg` as `init_cb`'s hidden third
  argument, as xscreensaver's `screenhack.c` does. Its table is empty until
  then. Resources the framework reads but a hack does not define
  (`delta3d`, `size`, ...) fall back to `kFrameworkDefaults` in
  `x11shim/resources.c`. A `HackEntry`'s `overrides` list beats the hack's own
  defaults (Galaxy runs with `count: -3`, at most three galaxies; a count of
  -2 or above skips the hack's restart cleanup and leaks); register it with
  `XLOCKMORE_HACK_WITH`. Galaxy, Drift, Discrete and Flame are built through
  `hacks/<name>_single.c`, which includes the framework headers, then
  `hacks/single_precision.h` (`double` and the libm calls become `float` and
  the `f` versions; the S3's FPU is single-precision only), then the unmodified
  hack; the original `.c` is excluded from each env's `build_src_filter`.
- Wide lines (`line_width` above 1), arcs and pixmap writes live in

`AFTER_DARK_IMAGE`) into a header in the build directory. Without the image
the hack is left out of the build. A firmware binary built with the image
contains the artwork, so do not publish one.

The tool reads the disk with `machfs` (MIT, <https://github.com/elliotnunn/machfs>),
which `uv` fetches when the tool runs; it is not copied into this repository.

### The Windows 95 screenshot

DecayScreen smears a picture of the screen, which xscreensaver grabs and the
board cannot. `firmware/assets/grab-image.png` stands in for it: a 640 by 480
screenshot of the Windows 95 desktop, downloaded from GUIdebook Gallery
(<https://guidebookgallery.org/pics/gui/desktop/full/win95.png>) and committed
unchanged. It shows Microsoft's interface and artwork, which are Microsoft's,
and it is not part of the MIT-licensed code in this repository. This project
has not checked what terms GUIdebook Gallery offers; it is included at Rod's
request. `firmware/grab_image.py` converts it to the raw blob described in
`ximage-loader.h` at build time. To use another picture, set `XS_GRAB_IMAGE`
to its file, or `none` for no picture.

"""PlatformIO pre-build script: turns the picture hacks "grab" into a header,
generated/grab_image.h in the build directory, that main.cpp hands to the shim
(xshim_set_grab_image). DecayScreen melts it; upstream grabs the screen.

The picture is firmware/assets/grab-image.png (a Windows 95 screenshot), or the
file named by XS_GRAB_IMAGE (relative paths are taken from the repository
root). It is scaled to fit 466 pixels (a 640 by 480 screenshot becomes 466 by
350, about 340 KB of flash). With XS_GRAB_IMAGE=none nothing is generated and
a hack that wants a picture loads nothing. Needs uv, because Pillow is not in
PlatformIO's Python."""

import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

Import("env")  # noqa: F821

project = Path(env["PROJECT_DIR"])  # noqa: F821
header = Path(env.subst("$BUILD_DIR")) / "generated" / "grab_image.h"  # noqa: F821
GRAB_SIZE = 466

choice = os.environ.get("XS_GRAB_IMAGE", "")
image = None
if choice != "none":
    image = Path(choice) if choice else project / "assets" / "grab-image.png"
    if not image.is_absolute():
        image = project.parent / image
    if not image.is_file():
        sys.exit(f"XS_GRAB_IMAGE={choice or 'default'}: no such file ({image})")

if image is None:
    header.unlink(missing_ok=True)
else:
    uv = shutil.which("uv")
    if not uv:
        raise SystemExit("the grab image needs uv on PATH to convert the image")
    subprocess.run(
        [
            uv,
            "run",
            str(project.parent / "tools" / "make_logo_blob.py"),
            str(image),
            "--name",
            "grab_image_blob",
            "--size",
            str(GRAB_SIZE),
            "-o",
            str(header),
        ],
        check=True,
    )
    print(f"Grab image: {image}")

"""Turn an image into the C header that Maze's logo is read from.

The device has no PNG decoder, so the image goes in as a raw RGB565 blob with
a 1-bit mask. The layout is documented in
firmware/src/x11shim/include/ximage-loader.h.

Run with: uv run tools/make_logo_blob.py logo-50.gif --name logo_50_png \\
    -o firmware/src/x11shim/include/images/gen/logo-50_png.h
"""

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

OPAQUE_ALPHA = 128


def rgb565(r: int, g: int, b: int) -> int:
    return (r & 0xF8) << 8 | (g & 0xFC) << 3 | b >> 3


def build_blob(width: int, height: int, rgba: bytes) -> bytes:
    if not (0 < width <= 0xFFFF and 0 < height <= 0xFFFF):
        raise ValueError(f"size {width}x{height} does not fit the blob header")
    if len(rgba) != width * height * 4:
        raise ValueError(f"expected {width * height * 4} RGBA bytes, got {len(rgba)}")

    pixels = bytearray()
    mask = bytearray()
    stride = (width + 7) // 8
    for y in range(height):
        row = bytearray(stride)
        for x in range(width):
            r, g, b, a = rgba[(y * width + x) * 4 :][:4]
            opaque = a >= OPAQUE_ALPHA
            pixels += (rgb565(r, g, b) if opaque else 0).to_bytes(2, "little")

# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.13"
# dependencies = ["pillow"]
# ///
"""Rasterise a TrueType font into the C header that the Xft stand-in draws from.

The device has no font renderer, so each size is drawn here once, as 8-bit
coverage for printable ASCII (32 to 126). The structures are declared in
firmware/src/x11shim/include/xft_font.h and handed to the shim with
xshim_set_font.

Run with: uv run tools/make_font_atlas.py firmware/assets/fonts/SpecialElite-Regular.ttf \\
    --name special_elite --sizes 12,16,20,24 -o special_elite.h
"""

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

FIRST, LAST = 32, 126
MIN_SIZE = 4


def build_glyph(font, ch: str, size: int, alpha: bytearray) -> dict:
    """Render ch tightly cropped, appending its coverage to alpha."""
    advance = round(font.getlength(ch))
    canvas = Image.new("L", (size * 3, size * 3), 0)
    ImageDraw.Draw(canvas).text((size, size * 2), ch, fill=255, font=font, anchor="ls")
    box = canvas.getbbox()
    if box is None:
        return {"w": 0, "h": 0, "left": 0, "top": 0, "advance": advance, "offset": 0}
    left, upper, right, lower = box
    ink = canvas.crop(box)
    offset = len(alpha)
    alpha += ink.tobytes()
    return {
        "w": right - left,
        "h": lower - upper,
        "left": left - size,
        "top": size * 2 - upper,
        "advance": advance,
        "offset": offset,
    }


def build_font(path: Path, sizes: list[int]) -> list[dict]:
    result = []
    for size in sizes:
        if size < MIN_SIZE:
            raise ValueError(f"size {size} is below {MIN_SIZE} pixels")
        try:
            font = ImageFont.truetype(str(path), size)
        except OSError as err:
            raise ValueError(f"{path}: not a usable font ({err})") from err
        ascent, descent = font.getmetrics()
        alpha = bytearray()
        glyphs = [
            build_glyph(font, chr(code), size, alpha) for code in range(FIRST, LAST + 1)
        ]
        result.append(
            {
                "pixel_size": size,
                "ascent": ascent,
                "descent": descent,
                "glyphs": glyphs,
                "alpha": bytes(alpha),
            }
        )
    return result


def c_bytes(data: bytes) -> str:
    rows = []
    for i in range(0, len(data), 24):
        rows.append("  " + ",".join(f"{b}" for b in data[i : i + 24]) + ",")
    return "\n".join(rows)


def c_header(name: str, font: list[dict], source: str) -> str:
    guard = f"GENERATED_{name.upper()}_H"
    out = [
        f"/* Generated by tools/make_font_atlas.py from {source}. Do not edit. */",
        f"#ifndef {guard}",
        f"#define {guard}",
        '#include "x11shim/xft_font.h"',
        "",
    ]
    for size in font:
        px = size["pixel_size"]
        out.append(f"static const unsigned char {name}_alpha_{px}[] = {{")
        out.append(c_bytes(size["alpha"]) if size["alpha"] else "  0,")
        out.append("};")
        out.append(f"static const XshimGlyph {name}_glyphs_{px}[] = {{")
        for g in size["glyphs"]:
            out.append(
                f"  {{{g['w']},{g['h']},{g['left']},{g['top']},"
                f"{g['advance']},{g['offset']}}},"
            )
        out.append("};")
    out.append(f"static const XshimFontSize {name}_sizes[] = {{")
    for size in font:
        px = size["pixel_size"]
        out.append(
            f"  {{{px},{size['ascent']},{size['descent']},"
            f"{name}_glyphs_{px},{name}_alpha_{px}}},"
        )
    out.append("};")
    out.append(
        f"static const XshimFont {name}_font = "
        f"{{{len(font)}, {name}_sizes}};"
    )
    out.append(f"#endif /* {guard} */")
    return "\n".join(out) + "\n"


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=(__doc__ or "").split("\n\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("ttf", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--name", required=True, help="C identifier prefix")

Ports XJack, and adds an Xft text stand-in to the shim so it can draw. Written
by Claude, an agent working under Rod's direction.

## What changed

- **XJack** is copied unmodified (checked with `cmp`) and built through
  `hacks/xjack_xft.c`, which includes the stand-in first. It is last in
  `g_hacks[]` before the After Dark toasters.
- **Xft stand-in** (`x11shim/xft.c`, `xft.h`, `xft_font.h`; ours, MIT). It
  loads a font by the nearest baked size, measures text, and draws
  pre-rasterised ASCII glyphs alpha-blended onto the canvas, clipped in 64 bits
  and marked dirty. Anything outside ASCII draws as `?`. With no font installed
  a hack gets a blank one, because XJack `abort()`s without a font and
  `test_pyro` and `test_push_present` replay every hack.
- **Special Elite** (Apache 2.0, from google/fonts) is committed unchanged with
  its licence in `firmware/assets/fonts/`, and has a section in
  `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. `tools/make_font_atlas.py` rasterises it at 12, 16,
  20 and 24 px at build time (`firmware/font_atlas.py`); `main.cpp` installs it.
  XJack defaults to 20 px (`-DXJACK_FONT_PX`): upstream's 12 was too small.
- **Wrapper fixes**, each with a test that fails without it. XJack clears the
  window, and the shim clears to black where `screenhack.c` uses the
  `background` resource, which gave black type on a black page. And
  `xjack_init` sizes the page before its margins, which xscreensaver corrects
  with a reshape after init: without one, lines typed at the bottom were
  clipped and scrolled up half drawn.
- Docs: the port-hack skill no longer lists Xft as unportable, and the shim and
  hack notes in `.claude/rules/` cover the stand-in and XJack.

## Verified

- **Compiles:** `pio run -e stopwatch` builds; flash is 88.8% of the app
  partition (87.0% before; the font tables are about 57 KB).
- **Host tests pass:** 741 of 741 native cases, 547 pytest (one skipped),
  `check_notices.py`, markdownlint, pre-commit. New tests are mutation-checked:
  20 of 22 mutants of `xft.c` die, and the two survivors only overflow
  off-canvas; 5 of 5 of the blank-font fallback; 8 of 8 of the font tool; and
  both wrapper fixes.
- **Runs on the device:** flashed pinned to XJack at 16 and then 20 px. Rod
  looked at it and said 20 looks good (colour, scrolling and layout).

## Not verified

- fps, step time and free heap and PSRAM on the board are unmeasured, and there
  is no row in `tools/assessment_measured.md.in` yet.
- No rotation soak with XJack in the registry.
- The pinned frame hash uses a blocky test font (`test_font.h`), so it does not
  follow FreeType; the real font is only seen on the panel.

## For Rod

- The runner sends no reshape and does not default the window background, which
  `screenhack.c` does. I fixed both in XJack's wrapper because changing the
  runner changes what every hack sees. Other light-background hacks that call
  `XClearWindow` may have the same fault: worth a look?
- `screenhack.h` does not include `xft.h`, for the same reason. The other Xft
  rows in the assessment (apollonian, fluidballs, memscroller, penetrate,
  noseguy) should now need only a wrapper like this one.
